title: Partition Museum Amritsar – A Journey Through India’s History
content:
Explore Partition Museum Amritsar

The Partition Museum in Amritsar offers a deep and emotional experience through stories of the people who lived through the 1947 Partition. With photographs, personal belongings, rare documents, and survivor testimonies, the museum preserves the memories of loss, courage, and hope. It is a must-visit destination for anyone who wants to understand India’s past and the real impact of Partition on millions of lives.

Why Visit the Partition Museum ?

  • Discover real stories from the 1947 Partition
  • Rare documents, audio recordings, and personal belongings showcased
  • Emotional galleries representing courage and survival
  • Beautifully designed heritage building near Town Hall
  • A perfect place for history lovers and students

History Behind the Museum

The Partition Museum was established to honour and remember those who faced one of the biggest migrations in human history in Amritsar, Punjab It represents the sacrifice, struggle, and hope of people who lost their homes but never gave up on life. The museum aims to keep these memories alive for future generations.

What’s Inside the Partition Museum

  • Interactive galleries with voice recordings of survivors
  • Artwork and newspaper clippings from the Partition era
  • Memorial installations including the Wall of Hope
  • Films and photographs that show the refugee journey
  • Calm and peaceful spaces for reflection and learning

 Information for Visitors

Entry Fee

  • Indian nationals: ₹ 10
  • Foreign nationals: ₹ 250 
  • Children under age 5: Free 
  • Admission is also free for Partition survivors.

Best Time to Visit

  • Morning or afternoon hours are best to explore calmly. 
  • Weekdays are recommended to avoid big crowds.

Nearby Place to visit

  • Make it a combined heritage tour:
  • Golden Temple
  • Jallianwala Bagh
  • Gobindgarh Fort
  • Wagah Border (in the evening)
excerpt: The Partition Museum in Amritsar is one of the most emotional and powerful places to visit in India. Dedicated to the Partition of 1947, it preserves stories, documents, photographs, and memories of the people who lived through the painful division of India and Pakistan. This museum is a must-visit for anyone who wants to understand our country’s past and its impact on millions of lives.
